title: Learning the Map
logline: Young novices memorise an ancient map of the mind, with 121 kinds of consciousness, by heart, long before they understand it.

object.note: Object 1 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The early sounds that mark the start of a day lead into a monastic school where the day begins with recitation: names learned for what happens inside.

thread_out.thread: The question left by the novices' memorised map, a name for everything inside, meets an outside mirror: a boat still called by one name though its planks have all been replaced.

requirements: A pirivena teaching Abhidhamma to young novices
Consent from guardians, teachers and the chief monk

suggestions.name: A village pirivena in the Kandy or Kegalle districts
suggestions.why: Many small monastic schools; hill landscape.
suggestions.verify: A specific school must be found and approached with care.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Long ago, teachers drew up a detailed map of the mind that sorts every kind of passing moment of awareness into 121 types, and young novices still learn it by heart before they understand it. The map describes the mind we feel as one steady thing as a very fast stream of separate moments, each knowing one thing.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අපට එකම සිතක් ලෙස දැනෙන්නේ ඉතා වේගයෙන් එකිනෙක ඉපිද නැතිවන සිත් පෙළක් බවත්, ඒ සිත් වර්ග 121කට බෙදා දක්වන සිතියම පොඩි හාමුදුරුවරු කටපාඩමින් උගන්නා බවත් මෙයින් පෙනේ.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma teaches that everything it describes falls into four ultimate realities (paramattha dhamma): mind (citta), the mental factors that arise with it, matter, and Nibbāna. Mind is described as the knowing of an object: it arises only with an object, takes one object at a time, and runs as a stream so fast and gapless that it feels like a single mind. Though mind is one in its nature, it is divided for teaching by plane (bhūmi) and by kind into 89 types or, in the fuller count, 121. One text tells the student to learn the 121 by heart, because further study depends on it.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film follows novices through chanting, memorising and being tested, a teacher's question met with a hesitant answer, handwritten charts, and ordinary play in between. The viewer notices the gap between reciting a name for what happens inside and actually seeing it, and that the map is carried in the body by repetition long before it is understood.

key_terms.en: mind; the knowing of an object
plane; the first way the mind is sorted

lesson.caution: The 121 types are kinds of passing moments, not personality types or a ladder of better and worse people, and the numbers themselves are not the point.
lesson.builds_on: After two films about names for things outside us, a mountain and a morning, this film turns to names for what happens inside, and lays out the map the whole series will walk through.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
